gate: Sampled extremum comparisons are BIASED TOWARD FALSE POSITIVES, not merely noisy (Harmonia-A soak P10)
eli5: Comparing max(col) against max(col::numeric) on a LIMIT sample does not just give you a wobbly answer, it gives you a wrong answer in a predictable DIRECTION: a divergence is resolved by whichever rare extreme value happens to sort highest both ways, and sampling is exactly the operation that drops rare rows, so sampled sweeps report MORE trap hits than exist. My own P4 sweep reported 14 divergent columns where the full table has 13 -- adelic_genus looked divergent only because none of the 96 rows holding '97' (out of 3.8 million) were drawn. The rule is that any max/min-based trap check must run full-table or with an explicit ORDER BY; a bigger sample does not fix a directional bias, and on this table a full scan cost 1.1 seconds per column, so the sampling was never buying anything.

gate: CORRECTION to my own P10 gate entry: sampling bias FLIPS SIGN with test polarity (Harmonia-A soak P11)
eli5: Last pass I parked a rule saying sampled extremum comparisons are biased toward false positives, and that is only half true, so the parked entry as written would mislead whoever picks it up. Dropping a rare extreme value creates an apparent divergence in a max-vs-max comparison (false POSITIVE, which is how P4 over-reported trap 1 by one column) but hides an overflow in an exceeds-a-threshold comparison (false NEGATIVE, which is how P9 under-reported trap 2 by one column). The usable rule is that unsampled aggregates -- counts, count-distinct, equality counts -- are deterministic and safe, while any check resting on a max or min must run full-table, because you cannot predict which way a sample will lie to you without first working out the test's polarity.

gate: zoo-matrix Checkpoint has an INVERTED robustness gradient — LOW reachability, trivial fix (Harmonia-A soak P18)
eli5: The checkpoint loader deliberately tolerates a half-written final line from a kill, which is the messy failure everyone expects, but the very next statement reads rec['examinee'] and rec['probe_id'] with no guard, so a line that is perfectly valid JSON and merely missing a key raises KeyError from the constructor and the checkpoint cannot be opened at all. That inverts the gradient: the more corrupt input is handled and the less corrupt one is fatal, and the blast radius is the whole resume rather than one lost row. Impact is genuinely LOW because record() always writes both keys and a mid-line kill produces truncation rather than a missing key, so this needs a hand-edit, a schema change or a second writer to fire -- the fix is one guarded access in harmonia/experiments/run_zoo_matrix.py, which is not mine to edit.

gate: gen_abs_extra_clean: at a==b the ground truth is INCOMPLETE (12.5% of probes) — Harmonia-A soak P19
eli5: The generator deliberately forces a<=b so that a root always exists and any 'no solution' answer is unambiguously an over-refusal, which is exactly the right guard for what it measures. But b = a + randint(0, 8) makes a==b reachable about one probe in eight, and at that boundary |x-a| = b-x collapses to |x-a| = a-x, which every x <= a satisfies -- so the true answer is a half-line while the recorded ground truth is the single point (a+b)/2. Any reasoner that correctly says 'all x at most a' would be graded wrong against a ground truth that is not merely different but incomplete, and since this generator feeds the H1 over-refusal measurement, the contamination sits in the arm the instrument exists to measure. Whether it actually bites depends on whether reasoners ever give the interval answer, which I did not measure; the file is harmonia/experiments/reasoning_phase0.py and is not mine to edit.

gate: What a second party CAN and CANNOT confirm about the new A5 tier (Harmonia-A soak P23)
eli5: A5 is a stronger verification tier than A4 because it rests on full text pulled out of the actual PDF rather than an abstract, and I checked the one A5 anchor that makes a mathematical claim: its quoted Theorem 1.2 is internally coherent, its 'upper matches lower iff p>=2r' remark is correct across 266 parameter pairs, and the theorem really does support the anchor's headline that the tensor constant grows polynomially rather than like sqrt(log d). What I could NOT check is the thing A5 actually asserts -- that the quote is verbatim -- because verifying fidelity means re-fetching the PDF and diffing the text, not reasoning about the formula. So an outside party can confirm an A5 anchor is self-consistent and correctly interpreted, and cannot confirm it was transcribed accurately, which is worth writing into the tier's definition so nobody reads a second opinion as more than it is.
